title: Section 80C Deductions: Full List & The ₹1.5 Lakh Limit Explained (FY 2025-26)

faq.a: Yes, Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) can claim deductions under Section 80C, provided the income is taxable in India and the investments are made in India.

faq.q: What happens if I invest more than ₹1.5 lakh under Section 80C?
faq.a: If your total eligible investments and expenses exceed ₹1.5 lakh, you can only claim a deduction up to the maximum limit of ₹1.5 lakh. The excess amount does not provide any further tax benefit under Section 80C.

faq.q: Is interest earned on PPF eligible for 80C deduction?
faq.a: No, the interest earned on PPF contributions is exempt from tax and does not qualify for a deduction under Section 80C. Only the contributions made to PPF are eligible for the deduction.

faq.q: Are contributions to NPS covered under Section 80C?
faq.a: Contributions to the National Pension System (NPS) Tier I account are covered under Section 80CCD(1) which is part of the overall Section 80C limit. Additionally, an exclusive deduction of up to ₹50,000 is available under Section 80CCD(1B) over and above the ₹1.5 lakh limit.

faq.q: Is the principal repayment of a second home loan also eligible for 80C?
faq.a: Yes, the principal repayment component of a home loan for a second house is also eligible for deduction under Section 80C, subject to the overall ₹1.5 lakh limit.

faq.q: Can I claim tuition fees for my spouse's education under 80C?
faq.a: No, Section 80C allows deduction for tuition fees paid for the education of up to two children. Tuition fees for your spouse's or your own education are not eligible for this deduction.

faq.q: What is the lock-in period for ELSS investments?
faq.a: Equity Linked Savings Schemes (ELSS) have a mandatory lock-in period of 3 years from the date of investment. This is the shortest lock-in period among all Section 80C investments.
